executive_assessment.text: New evidence differentiates donor-basin water injustice and supply stress in Khuzestan and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari from drought-related political responses in Isfahan and Hamedan. Water policy and climate effects are not disentangled.

Khuzestan aquifer observations add named local water-system vulnerabilities around Dezful and Andimeshk, but the measurements end in2018. They must not be presented as a current household-access assessment.

geographic_notes.text: The author argues that transfers from western and southern donor basins toward central Iran have damaged donor-area water systems and heightened center-periphery tensions.
The2024 article reports tanker dependence in over200villages of Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari and salinity-related water and date-palm losses in Khuzestan, drawing on cited historical sources.
The author reports that disagreements over inter-basin transfers and their perceived inequities have accompanied local protest and sociopolitical tension.
The study contrasts farmer mobilization around drought and water allocation in Isfahan with an absence of comparable protest in Hamedan.
The author argues that drought-related water problems can reduce political trust and that weak water-governance responses shape local contention.
For2008–2018, the Khuzestan study identifies groundwater decline in eastern/northeastern aquifers and drawdown up to33metres around Dezful and Andimeshk.

known_gaps.text: Climate projections: the official 2015 INDC contains 2030 temperature and runoff projections but does not identify an underlying model or scenario in the inspected passage. A modern source-accessible CMIP6 national and subnational set is needed.
Rainfall attribution: WWA's attribution is strong for warming-related SPEI severity, but its rainfall-only estimate includes no-change possibilities.

Geographic/population gaps: Nationally representative evidence on differentiated vulnerability by gender, income, ethnicity, disability, rural/urban status and migration status is incomplete. Current studies are often basin- or programme-specific.
Causal Climate-FCV evidence: the ZayandehRud study is subnational and perception-based. No verified national study in this set demonstrates a climate effect on conflict.
FCV-to-climate strength: policy and macroeconomic evidence supports mechanisms through sanctions, finance, technology, infrastructure and trade, but does not quantify adaptation delays or losses.
Evaluation: a terminal evaluation was publicly procured for a wetland component, but the final independent report was not located. Programme figures are therefore implementer-reported.

Unintended effects: Evidence is weak on rebound effects - for example whether water-efficiency gains lead to expanded irrigated acreage or total consumption - and on winners/losers from allocation or conservation programmes.
Water-use statistics: FAO and WWA use different agriculture-withdrawal/consumption figures and metrics. The discrepancy is unresolved and neither figure should be substituted for the other.

Dust and land degradation: The national policy and WWA discuss dust/desertification, but this packet does not establish the relative contributions of climate, land use, wetland loss, salinization and other anthropogenic drivers well enough for a strong attribution claim.

Current conflict and infrastructure: World Bank evidence describes disruption and damaged infrastructure, but granular sector evidence separating direct damage from chronic underinvestment, sanctions and water scarcity is needed.
Coastal risk: Coastal pressures were a country priority, but sufficiently detailed, accessible and locatable Iranian coastal/sea-level evidence was not secured in the final verified source set.

Refugee hosting and mobility: rolling UNHCR figures changed by October 2026, and the original end-2025 and 1 August 2026 values were not recoverable from an archived primary passage. They are excluded pending a dated source.
The inspected sources cluster around Khuzestan and central/inter-basin water disputes; current original subnational evidence is thinner for other provinces.
Conflict-related restrictions on climate adaptation were not substantiated by an additional accessible primary source in this search batch.
The GCF adaptation document and a Lake Urmia article search were blocked, so no claims from them are included.
Two Crisis Group claims were withheld because no primary publisher passage could be opened; the search/staging access history remains in the intake audit.
New hydrogeological observations cover2008–2018 and policy studies2024–2025; they do not establish2026conditions.
No additional complete climate-attributed pathway was inferred from water-allocation disputes: abstraction, governance and climate pressures are not interchangeable.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
